U.S. equity markets opened mixed to flat today, following yesterday's 500 point swing in the Dow from peak to trough. While the markets did close in negative territory, what we saw was a significant snap-back rally as all the major indexes climbed back over 1.5% from yesterday's morning's lows on strong volume. Currently markets have turned negative again, but the trading volume for now indicate a below average day which could be a sign of consolidation or worse, a continuation of the negative trend. Currently 8 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are trading lower with Communications and Materials the worst performing sectors. Oil is trading higher following mixed EIA storage data. Gold trades lower while the dollar is higher. The yield on the 10-yr has slipped for a second day in a row to 3.1186.
The S&P 500 has closed lower 13 of the 17 trading sessions so far this month and is currently tracking lower for a 6th day in a row. The index has retreated 7.5% since its 52 week high of 2940.91 made on September 21st, barely one month ago. The index now clings to 1.2% increase year to date. It is hard to think we were writing about the longest U.S. bull market in history in August! Over 65 members of the S&P 500 have made new 52 week lows this week. The recent selloff has been broad based as Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Energy, Industrials and Materials have had the largest names. Mega-cap names such as C, ABBV, DWDP, BMY, CAT, CCL and SLB are a few than have dragged the index lower. Notably missing here are Technology and mega-cap Consumer names. Earnings for tech has started but the behemoths who have the highest weightings in the index, start reporting tonight. We shall wait to see if names such as GOOGL, MSFT, INTC, AMZN, TSL who report this week and AAPL next week can help stop this skid.

Brian's Technical Take
Yesterday the S&P 500 was deep in the red while bottoming at 2,691 on an intraday basis. This temporarily broke down below the prior low from mid-October, 2,710, but then the flagship large cap index rallied a phenomenal 50 points to its closing level of 2,741.
The potential here is that a significant low was just made, a "double bottom" in technical jargon, from which we could see a sharp recovery into he end of the year. The "double bottom" is exactly what we saw in the summer of 2015 and Q1'16. While it is certainly no guarantee we see another one this time around, for many investors the setup is already there and more importantly, the risk levels are clearly defined. Selloffs are difficult to bottom tick but when there is no guessing, rather a "set it and forget it", when you know your risk levels. In the bull's favor are some bullish divergences with both the daily RSI, as well as the percentage of stocks making new 52-week lows, each making a higher low vs earlier this month.
Click the image for larger view
Markets continue to slide as macro and political headlines breed uncertainty in the markets. Trading volumes yesterday were good, showing strength in the market rally, but today's slippage, on average volumes shows investor sentiment has not completely changed and caution still prevails. Traders await big name Tech and Consumer names to report this week. If investor reaction to the mega-cap numbers is good over the next few days, this market weakness should end.
